topic.title: Michigan Funding & Resources
topic.description: Verified Michigan funding and support programs — women’s grants, trans funds, LGBT+ referral, small-business help, and family emergency aid — with deadlines, fees, exclusions, and current application status read from official pages on 2026-10-03.

beginner.label: Beginner 🌱
beginner.tagline: Every entry below is a resource read from its official page on 2026-10-03 — what it gives, who qualifies, when it closes, what it costs, and whether it is open right now.
goals: Match a need to the right program: business grant, trans fund, referral line, or emergency aid
Know each deadline and fee before applying, including the Amber hardship waiver route
Check live application status first — THAW was paused and the 2026 pitch season concluded
Spot industry and eligibility exclusions, including the WomanUp adult-entertainment bar

concepts.title: Women — Business Funding
concepts.text:
Two funding routes for women-owned businesses, both read from the official program pages on 2026-10-03: a national monthly grant with a hardship fee waiver, and a Michigan pitch competition whose 2027 cycle closes Oct 4 2026.

- Amber Grant (WomensNet) — $10,000 monthly grants plus Startup and Business-Category grants, 3 x $50,000 year-end grants, $510,000 awarded across 2026 — eligibility: women 18+ who own at least 50% of a business based in the United States or Canada — deadline: monthly cycle from the 1st through 11:59 PM Eastern on the last day (next cutoff Oct 31 2026) — fee: $15 per application, non-refundable, with a hardship fee waiver available by emailing info@ambergrantsforwomen.com before applying — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://ambergrantsforwomen.com/get-an-amber-grant/
- WomanUp & Pitch Competition (Michigan Women Forward) — prizes per regional competition of $10,000, $5,000, $2,500, and $1,000 plus $1,000 audience choice, and $500 each for the top-50 non-placers — eligibility: Michigan-based, for-profit, at least 51% woman-owned, in the Idea/Startup track (under 3 years and under $150k revenue) or the Established/Growth track — deadline: 2027 cycle opened Aug 10 2026 and closes Oct 4 2026 at 11:59 PM, competitions run Feb 2 to Mar 2 2027 — fee: $20 with a 2-page concept paper, no waiver stated — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://miwf.org/business-programs/womanup-pitch/

⚠ WomanUp & Pitch industry exclusion: businesses in the cannabis, weapons, or adult entertainment industries are not eligible to participate — current employees of Michigan Women Forward and Consumers Energy are excluded as well, and prior non-winning finalists must wait one year. The 2027-cycle window closes Oct 4 2026 at 11:59 PM, with competitions Feb 2 to Mar 2 2027.

⚠ Verified 2026-10-03 against official pages.

concepts.title: Trans — Direct Funds
concepts.text:
Direct funds for trans and nonbinary people, plus the Michigan-specific entry point. The Trans Lifeline microgrants and both Point of Pride funds were read from official pages on 2026-10-03; the microgrants require no diagnosis, insurance, or income gate.

- Trans Lifeline Microgrants — cash toward legal and document-update fees such as name and gender-marker costs; amount not published, $100,000 moved in 2025 through 5 partner organizations — eligibility: trans and nonbinary people of any age, with no diagnosis, insurance, or income gate and no receipts or proof of use required — deadline: rolling, processed chronologically, stated wait 2-4 weeks, 48 applications processed per month — fee: $0 to apply — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://translifeline.org/microgrants/
- Point of Pride Annual Transgender Surgery Fund — direct financial assistance toward gender-affirming surgery, award amount not published — eligibility: transgender (FTM, MTF, non-binary, genderqueer, gender non-conforming, and all other non-cis identities), 18+ at time of surgery, financial need, surgery in the US with a US-based surgeon — deadline: applications open Nov 1 and close Nov 30 at 11:59 PM EST, surgery on or after March 1 of the following year, next window opens Nov 1 2026 — fee: $0 — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://www.pointofpride.org/annual-transgender-surgery-fund
- Point of Pride HRT Access Fund — 18 months of HRT-related care in kind: telemed visits, 6 lab visits, Uber vouchers, gender-marker letters, and prescription cost coverage — eligibility: trans or non-cis identity, financial need, live in the United States, at least 18 by Aug 1 2026, and meet the chosen telehealth provider's requirements — deadline: annual window May 1 to May 31, the 2026 window is closed and the next window is May 2027 — fee: $0 — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://www.pointofpride.org/hrt-access-fund
- Transgender Michigan — advocacy, support, education, and community events (Health Fair Oct 24, party Oct 31, Transgender Job Fair Nov 11 2026), no cash grants on the page — eligibility: mission serves transgender and gender non-conforming communities across Michigan — deadline: ongoing resource — fee: no fee stated — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://www.transgendermichigan.org/

⚠ Point of Pride windows are annual: the Surgery Fund opens Nov 1 and closes Nov 30 at 11:59 PM EST, and the HRT Access Fund runs May 1 to May 31. The HRT fund pays in kind rather than cash, and each partner provider only serves states inside its licensed area — confirm the provider covers Michigan.

⚠ Verified 2026-10-03 against official pages.

concepts.title: LGBT+ — Support & Referral
concepts.text:
Free support and referral entry points rather than cash grants. Both pages were read on 2026-10-03 and both are open to Michigan residents.

- Equality Michigan (EQMI) — education, victim services, and outreach statewide, no direct grants on the page — eligibility: LGBTQ+ neighbors throughout Michigan — deadline: ongoing — fee: no fee stated, services are free and the page solicits donations — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://www.equalitymi.org/
- LGBT National Hotline — free and confidential peer support, information, and local resources at 888-843-4564, with a Coming Out line at 888-688-5428 — eligibility: support volunteers identify as part of the LGBTQIA+ family and serve callers of all ages — deadline: ongoing, the lines are live — fee: $0 — trans status: explicit-inclusive — https://www.lgbthotline.org/

⚠ These are referral and support resources, not funding. Only Equality Michigan's homepage was read on 2026-10-03, so deeper service details on its sub-pages are unconfirmed — verify at equalitymi.org before describing specific services.

⚠ Verified 2026-10-03 against official pages.

concepts.title: Small Business — Michigan
concepts.text:
Michigan's free business-support network, two state and federal funding gateways, and one pitch competition to watch. Three of these five entries are free services rather than grants.

- Michigan SBDC (MI-SBDC) — no-cost consulting, training, market research, and grant-readiness help for new and existing small businesses; the SBDC disburses no grants itself — eligibility: any new venture or existing small business — deadline: ongoing, no deadline — fee: $0 (no-cost consulting) — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://sbdcmichigan.org/our-services
- MEDC 'I Need Funding' (Michigan Economic Development Corporation) — Michigan Supplier Conversion Grant ($31.8M federal pool for retooling), Capital Access loans routed through third-party lenders, and Match on Main reimbursement grants for downtown micro businesses — eligibility: 'MEDC offers funding resources to companies at all stages'; Supplier Conversion is restricted to current small and medium manufacturers of internal-combustion-engine vehicle parts — deadline: Supplier Conversion Notices of Intent being accepted as of 2026-10-03, Match on Main rounds are set by local partners with exact dates not stated on the page — fee: $0 to apply — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://www.michiganbusiness.org/services/funding/
- SCORE Michigan (free mentoring) — free 1:1 mentoring, workshops, and templates from an SBA resource partner, with the Michigan chapter index at https://www.score.org/mi/ — eligibility: 'a free service offered to any aspiring or established owners of a U.S.-based business' — deadline: ongoing, no deadline — fee: $0 — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://www.score.org/how-mentoring-works/
- SBA Michigan District Office — federal guaranteed-loan programs, counseling, federal contracting certifications, and disaster recovery assistance, serving the entire state of Michigan — eligibility: help with SBA funding programs, counseling, certifications, and disaster recovery; SBA loans are credit-based through private lenders — deadline: ongoing, program-specific cycles — fee: $0 for counseling and referrals, lender and guaranty fees can attach to loans — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://legacy.sba.gov/district/michigan
- Michigan's Next Big Idea Pitch Competition (Michigan Celebrates Small Business) — $10,000 cash prize, 2026 winner Zo's Mini Donuts, sponsored by Comcast Business with the Small Business Association of Michigan — eligibility: existing Michigan-based businesses ready to scale, with full 2027 rules not yet posted — deadline: the 2026 cycle has concluded and 2027 application dates are not yet posted — fee: no fee stated — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://michigancelebrates.org/2026-pitch-competition/

⚠ Michigan's Next Big Idea Pitch Competition: the 2026 cycle has concluded and 2027 application dates are not yet posted, so do not present it as open. MEDC round deadlines are set by local partners and must be confirmed before anyone applies.

⚠ Verified 2026-10-03 against official pages.

concepts.title: Families — Emergency Help
concepts.text:
Emergency help for Michigan households: state relief, one-call referral, energy-bill assistance, and one fund currently paused for new applications. All four pages were read on 2026-10-03.

- MDHHS State Emergency Relief (SER) — immediate help for heat and utilities, home repairs, relocation assistance, home ownership services, and burial — eligibility: 'provides immediate help to individuals and families facing conditions of extreme hardship or for emergencies that threaten health and safety', designed for low-income households that can normally meet their needs, with eligibility determined by the local MDHHS office — deadline: rolling emergency help with no application deadline, and not an appropriate solution to ongoing or chronic financial difficulty — fee: $0 (state benefit) — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://www.michigan.gov/mdhhs/assistance-programs/emergency-relief/overview/ser
- Michigan 211 — referral gateway to 27,000+ programs covering utilities, food, clothing, transportation, housing, HIV/STI services, grief and bereavement, and more; call 2-1-1 or 844-875-9211, text available — eligibility: open to any Michigan resident with no income gate stated — deadline: ongoing, the line is staffed — fee: $0 — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://mi211.org/get-help
- Michigan Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) — payment or partial payment of home energy bills (electricity, natural gas, propane, heating oil, other deliverable fuel) through an affordable monthly payment plan or a one-time direct payment — eligibility: eligible low-income households for their primary residence, income eligibility applies, applied for through local agencies or 211 — deadline: heating-season program year with no fixed deadline posted on the fetched page — fee: $0 — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://www.michigan.gov/mpsc/consumer/energy-assistance
- The Heat and Warmth Fund (THAW) — energy bill payment assistance as a MEAP partner, either an affordable monthly payment plan or a one-time direct payment toward the energy bill — eligibility: Michigan residents seeking energy bill payment assistance, with income qualification through MEAP — deadline: status as fetched 2026-10-03, temporarily not accepting new applications because of high demand, site directs users to 2-1-1 and MEAP — fee: $0 — trans status: criteria-clean-no-gate — https://thawfund.org/

⚠ THAW status caution: as fetched on 2026-10-03, THAW was temporarily not accepting new applications because of high demand and points visitors to 2-1-1 (mi211.org) and MEAP — check thawfund.org before applying, and use Michigan 211 or MEAP meanwhile.

⚠ Verified 2026-10-03 against official pages.

examples.title: Applying with a tight budget
examples.text: The Amber Grant charges $15 per application. If that fee creates a financial hardship, email info@ambergrantsforwomen.com BEFORE applying to request a fee waiver — the fee is non-refundable once paid, and one application covers every grant type.

examples.title: Energy bill due and THAW is paused
examples.text: As fetched 2026-10-03, THAW was not accepting new applications. The route that stays open: call 2-1-1 (or 844-875-9211) for Michigan 211 referral, or apply through a local MEAP agency for payment or partial payment of the home energy bill.

pitfalls.title: Treating a paused fund as gone
pitfalls.text: ⚠ THAW is temporarily closed to new applications, not defunct — the status can change, so re-check thawfund.org instead of assuming it is permanently unavailable.

pitfalls.title: Applying to a concluded competition
pitfalls.text: ⚠ Michigan’s Next Big Idea Pitch Competition finished its 2026 cycle and has not posted 2027 dates; WomanUp & Pitch is the live Michigan route, closing Oct 4 2026 at 11:59 PM.

exercises.title: Build a Michigan shortlist
exercises.text: Pick one need (business, trans care, family emergency) and list the two best entries for it from this page, with each deadline and fee written out from the bullet.

exercises.title: Verify one entry yourself
exercises.text: Open one official URL from this page and confirm its deadline or status line still matches what is written here; note the date you checked.

glossary.definition: MDHHS crisis help for heat and utilities, home repairs, relocation, home ownership services, and burial — rolling, with eligibility set by the local office.
Michigan Energy Assistance Program — pays or partly pays home energy bills for the primary residence via a monthly payment plan or one-time direct payment.
The Heat and Warmth Fund — a MEAP partner delivering energy bill assistance; temporarily not accepting new applications as fetched 2026-10-03.
Small Business Development Center — no-cost consulting, training, and market research; grants no money itself.
Michigan Economic Development Corporation — state funding portal listing grants, capital-access loans, and Match on Main reimbursement grants.

beginner.question: Which women's funding program explicitly excludes businesses in the adult entertainment industry?
options: Michigan's Next Big Idea Pitch Competition
beginner.explanation: The official WomanUp & Pitch page states that businesses in the cannabis, weapons, or adult entertainment industries are not eligible; the Amber Grant rules carry no such industry exclusion.

beginner.question: Which fund covers legal-document costs such as name and gender-marker updates?
options: Point of Pride HRT Access Fund
beginner.explanation: Trans Lifeline Microgrants pay toward legal and document-update fees, cost nothing to apply, and require no receipts or proof of use; the HRT Access Fund covers hormone care, THAW covers energy bills, and the SBDC is consulting only.

beginner.question: How do you request the Amber Grant fee waiver?
options: Call the WomensNet hotline after applying
No waiver exists — the $15 fee is absolute
beginner.explanation: The rules say that if the $15 fee creates a financial hardship, a fee waiver application may be requested, prior to applying, by emailing info@ambergrantsforwomen.com.

beginner.question: What does MDHHS State Emergency Relief (SER) cover?
options: Childcare subsidies and WIC food packages
Heat and utilities, home repairs, relocation assistance, home ownership services, and burial
Small business payroll and commercial rent
beginner.explanation: SER provides immediate help for heat and utilities, home repairs, relocation assistance, home ownership services, and burial for households facing extreme hardship or an emergency threatening health and safety.

beginner.question: What does the Michigan Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) pay?
options: Home energy bills — electricity, natural gas, propane, heating oil, and other deliverable fuel
beginner.explanation: MEAP reduces energy insecurity by paying or partly paying home energy costs for the primary residence, either through an affordable monthly payment plan or a one-time direct payment.

beginner.question: When does the Point of Pride Annual Transgender Surgery Fund accept applications?
options: Nov 1 to Nov 30 at 11:59 PM EST
beginner.explanation: Applications open Nov 1 and close Nov 30 at 11:59 PM EST, and surgery must happen on or after March 1 of the following year; the May window belongs to the Point of Pride HRT Access Fund.

beginner.question: How does the Point of Pride HRT Access Fund deliver its 18 months of support?
options: As a cash payment sent to the recipient
As a debit card loaded monthly
In kind — telemed visits, lab visits, Uber vouchers, gender-marker letters, and prescription cost coverage
As a tax credit claimed at filing
beginner.explanation: The HRT Access Fund is in-kind care delivered through partner telehealth providers (visits, labs, ride vouchers, letters, prescriptions) rather than cash, and only inside each provider's licensed service area.

beginner.question: Which single contact point searches more than 27,000 Michigan programs?
beginner.explanation: Michigan 211's database lists 27,000+ programs across utilities, food, housing, transportation, and more; SCORE mentors businesses, the SBA District Office handles federal programs, and Equality Michigan is advocacy and victim services.

beginner.question: As fetched on 2026-10-03, THAW was temporarily not accepting new energy-bill assistance applications.
beginner.explanation: THAW's homepage said high demand had paused new applications and directed people to 2-1-1 (mi211.org) and MEAP — check back before applying.

beginner.question: The Michigan SBDC charges small businesses a fee for its consulting services.
beginner.explanation: The Michigan SBDC advertises no-cost consulting, training, and market research; it charges nothing for advising and disburses no grants itself.
